1Purpose

This policy sets out what [Provider name] commits to once a participant's is written. We make sure the people who will carry out the plan understand it and are in it. We make sure they get help when something gets in the way. It is for participants, their families and supporters, the providers who carry out our plans, our practitioners and the people who check our work.

2Applies to

  • Every behaviour support plan that [Provider name] writes, interim or comprehensive, whether or not it includes a .
  • Every who works for us, employed or contracted.
  • Our work with every provider that carries out one of our plans, and with the of each participant.

POL-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Policy covers how we write a plan and give it out. This policy covers our work with providers while we draft the plan and everything after we give it out. Only a specialist behaviour support provider uses this policy. A provider that only carries out plans uses POL-BSP-04 Behaviour Support Plan Implementation Policy. Where we also carry out a plan with our own workers, both policies apply. We treat our own workers as we treat any other .

"The Restrictive Practices Rules" in this policy means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.

3Commitments

C1

We will develop every plan with the providers that will carry it out. We consult each before we draft, send each the draft and ask it to accept its part. We confirm that each has accepted before we hand the plan over.

We teach the positive strategies first. Each implementing provider trains and observes its own workers against the plan and confirms to us in writing which workers are competent. We observe a sample of workers carrying out the strategies and coach where we see a gap. We observe directly every worker who will apply a physical restraint protocol.

A physical restraint technique, and any as-needed practice, is not applied by an untrained worker, who calls the provider's on-call manager instead.

4Ground rules

G1

Every time limit in these commitments is our standard. The law sets none of them.

G2

This policy and its procedure authorise no restrictive practice. comes from the state or territory. A plan alone does not authorise a practice.

G3

We write down the source and the date for every authorisation rule we explain. The source is our state or territory note, last checked within the last 6 months and re-checked whenever the NDIS Commission or the state or territory body announces a change (PRO-SBS-02 Restrictive Practices Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support), step 2; our standard). It is not memory or a summary in this template, because the rules change and differ in each place.

G4

Specialist behaviour support is provided only by an NDIS behaviour support practitioner (Restrictive Practices Rules s 17). So only a practitioner explains the reasons for a plan, teaches its strategies and judges how well people carry them out. Other staff book sessions, send papers and file records.

G5

A worker is trained when their implementing provider has trained and observed them against the plan and confirmed it to us in writing, or when we have observed them ourselves. Attendance and a signature alone are not enough.

G6

A practitioner teaches a physical technique only if they are qualified to teach it. Otherwise a qualified trainer teaches it. Whenever another trainer teaches part of a plan, we check what they teach against the plan.

G7

We do not direct another provider's workers. We tell the provider in writing what we recommend and what we saw.

G8

The participant is the first person we explain a plan to. We ask what they think and we record their words.

G9

In a sole practitioner business, the Practitioner holds the Service Manager, , Quality Manager and Chief Executive roles and does what those roles do, with two exceptions. The external , engaged in writing and named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register, does the Service Manager's checks on the Practitioner's own work, and makes any reportable-incident decision with the Practitioner. REG-GOV-01 also names a cover Practitioner, who must be an NDIS behaviour support practitioner, and an independent contact for concerns, who hears any concern about the Practitioner and reads the sample of records. The Clinical Supervisor names the cover Practitioner in writing before any planned leave.

G10

Anyone can raise a concern or a complaint about how we have handled a plan. POL-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Policy applies. A concern about harm to a person goes to POL-SGD-01 Violence, Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation and Discrimination Policy.

G11

Paper copies work when systems are down.

9Words we use

460 words
behaviour support plan
the plan a behaviour support practitioner writes with a participant to meet their behaviour support needs. An interim plan covers an immediate need. A comprehensive plan follows a full assessment.
behaviour support practitioner
a person the NDIS Commissioner considers suitable to do behaviour support assessments and write plans that may include restrictive practices.
Clinical Lead
the senior Practitioner who owns clinical practice at [Provider name]. In a sole practitioner business, the Practitioner.
Clinical Supervisor
the experienced Practitioner who supervises a Practitioner's work and checks it. In a sole practitioner business, always someone outside [Provider name], engaged in writing.
trained
a worker is trained when their implementing provider has trained and observed them against the plan and confirmed it to us in writing, or when we have observed them ourselves.
implementing provider
any provider, registered or not, that delivers supports to the participant where the plan applies.
implementation contact
the person an implementing provider names as our contact for the plan.
support network
the family, friends, carers, guardian and advocates the participant chooses.
regulated restrictive practice
seclusion, chemical restraint, mechanical restraint, physical restraint or environmental restraint, as the Restrictive Practices Rules define them. Examples are a locked cupboard, a medicine given mainly to change behaviour, and bed rails that stop movement.
authorisation
the approval a state or territory requires before a regulated restrictive practice is used, however it is described. It can be consent, a decision by a panel or tribunal, or approval by an authorised officer.
instructions and guidance
what we give each person so they can carry out the plan. Examples are a strategy card for workers and a version of the plan the participant can use.
state or territory note
our one page for each state or territory where we work, kept in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register. It names the authorising body, who applies and what evidence is lodged. It carries its sources and the date it was last checked.
authorisation summary
one page for each practice that we give an implementing provider. It says who authorises the practice, who applies, what evidence is lodged and what conditions apply. The written notice we give under PRO-SBS-02 is this summary.
reporting summary
one page that lists the reporting duties of an implementing provider under the Restrictive Practices Rules and who holds each.
barrier
anything that stops a plan being followed as written.
say it back
asking a person to explain or show, in their own words, what they understood.
given out
a plan is given out when the participant, and with consent the support network and each implementing provider, hold the finished plan.
business day
a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

1Purpose

The result: every participant we assess gets an assessment that finds their unmet needs and the function of their behaviour. They get a plan written with them and with the people who carry it out. Those providers accept it, and a plan with a reaches the Commissioner on time.

This procedure gives effect to POL-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Policy, C1 to C14.

"Behaviour Support Rules" means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.

2When and who

Start this procedure when:

  • we receive a referral for a behaviour support assessment or plan
  • we take over a participant from another specialist provider
  • a review under PRO-SBS-04 Behaviour Support Plan Monitoring and Review Procedure says a plan must change, or the assessment revisit date is within 30 days.

Only a specialist behaviour support provider uses this procedure. A provider that only carries out plans uses PRO-BSP-05 Supporting the Assessment and Development of Behaviour Support Plans Procedure.

Who acts:

  • The Service Manager logs the referral, sets the dates, allocates the people, prepares each lodgement and keeps the register.
  • The triages the risk.
  • The Practitioner does every assessment, writes every plan and lodges it in the Commission's portal.
  • The checks each report and each plan.
  • The Quality Manager and the Chief Executive check the register and receive anything late. The Quality Manager decides whether an incident is reportable and notifies the Commission.

In a small provider one person may hold several roles. A sole Practitioner holds the Service Manager, Quality Manager and Chief Executive roles, except that the decision whether an incident is reportable is made by the outside Clinical Supervisor with them. The Clinical Supervisor is always someone outside, is the Clinical Lead for this procedure, and does the Service Manager's checks on the sole Practitioner's own work. Where a step says to tell another role, a sole Practitioner writes it on the plan row and tells the Clinical Supervisor.

Terms in this procedure:

  • Practitioner: an NDIS , a person the Commissioner considers suitable to assess behaviour and write plans (Behaviour Support Rules, section 5).
  • plan: a , interim or comprehensive.
  • assessment report: the written record of the assessment, on FRM-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessment Report Template.
  • cover sheet: the record of how a plan was checked, shared and lodged, on FRM-BSP-02 Behaviour Support Plan Cover Sheet and Lodgement Record.
  • plan row: one line of REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register for one plan version.
  • : a provider that carries out the strategies in a plan.
  • regulated restrictive practice: seclusion, chemical restraint, mechanical restraint, physical restraint or environmental restraint (Behaviour Support Rules, section 6).
  • engagement date: the date we agree in writing to develop the plan, or the date a regulated restrictive practice was first used, whichever is earlier (POL-SBS-03 ground rule 7). Where that use was before the referral reached us, the date the referral reached us. A later date named in a service agreement never moves it.
  • in force: a plan is in force from the date the Practitioner finalises and signs it.

3Before you start

  • You are a Practitioner the Commissioner considers suitable, or you are supporting one.
  • You can open REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register.
  • You have FRM-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessment Report Template and FRM-BSP-02 Behaviour Support Plan Cover Sheet and Lodgement Record, on paper or in the system.
  • You have the participant's communication preferences: FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form.
  • You know where FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form is kept.
  • You know your Clinical Supervisor's name and how to reach them.
  • You know the state or territory where the participant lives. Its law decides who can consent and which practices need .

4Watch out

  • If anyone is in danger, call 000 first. Tell the Service Manager after. A delay can cost a life.
  • Only a suitable Practitioner may assess or write. Anyone else doing it breaks a condition of our registration (Behaviour Support Rules, sections 17 and 18).
  • No consent, no assessment. Gathering information without valid consent breaches the participant's privacy and their right to decide.
  • Look for pain and illness first. A plan built on the wrong cause leaves the participant in pain and does not work.
  • The clocks start at engagement. Where a regulated restrictive practice led to our engagement, missing the 1 month or the 6 month limit breaks a condition of registration (Behaviour Support Rules, section 19).
  • A restrictive practice never enters through the back door. One that reaches a plan without consultation, notice and authorisation can be used on the participant unlawfully.
  • Lodge whether or not the practice is authorised. The Rules ask for the plan either way (Behaviour Support Rules, section 24(2)).
  • A plan nobody accepted may not be followed. Workers who have not seen it may respond in unsafe or uneven ways.

Get consent

Step 6

Warning. A family member, carer or provider cannot consent for an adult unless they hold legal authority. Collecting or sharing information without valid consent breaches the participant's privacy and their right to decide.

Practitioner

Ask the participant for consent.

Meet the participant in the way that suits them. Use their communication preferences. Explain what the assessment is, what we will collect, from whom, who will see it, and that they can stop at any time. Use Decision table 2 to find who decides. Offer an independent advocate. Ask for consent to assess, to ask named people and services for information, and to share the report. FRM-SBS-03 Q9 to Q14

Before you collect any information. First meeting within 10 business days of the engagement date (our standard)

Assess

Step 7

Warning. A behaviour can be the only way a participant can say they are in pain or unwell. A plan built on the wrong cause leaves the participant in pain and will not work.

Practitioner

Ask for a health review.

With consent, ask the participant's doctor or another health practitioner to review pain, illness, medicines and their side effects, sleep, hearing, vision, sensory needs and mental health. Do not diagnose. Do not advise a change of medicine. Only the prescriber decides that. If the review cannot happen quickly, record what you asked, of whom and when.

Result
A health practitioner has looked for health causes, or a dated request is on record with a date to chase it.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q24
Time limit
Ask within 5 business days of consent (our standard)
Step 8

Practitioner

Ask for what is already known.

With consent, ask for earlier assessments and plans, allied health and medical reports, school or day service records, and assessments by other providers and mainstream services. Ask each implementing provider for its incident reports and behaviour records (FRM-BSP-04 Behaviour Record). If we are taking over from another specialist provider, ask for the current plan, its lodgement and authorisation details and its data. Our own clocks still run from our engagement date. Record what you asked for and what arrived.

Result
Every source is listed with its date, and each gap is written down.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q16, Q18 to Q20
Time limit
Within 10 business days of consent (our standard)
Step 9

Practitioner

Collect direct and indirect data.

Watch the participant yourself in each setting where the behaviour happens, at the times it happens. Interview the participant, their and workers. Use behaviour charts and rating tools. Record the period and the settings, and say why they are long enough. Workers and family supply records. They do not assess.

Result
The assessment rests on what you saw and what people told you, from every setting.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q15, Q17
Time limit
Finish before the assessment report is due, 49 days after the engagement date (our standard)
Step 10

Practitioner

Ask the participant what matters to them.

Ask in their way and in their words. Cover their strengths, likes and goals, what is going well and what is not, culture and language, how they communicate, their history, and what home and routines are like. Ask only about history they choose to share. If the participant is Aboriginal or Torres Strait Islander, ask who in their community they want to advise us.

Result
The assessment is about the whole person, their own words are in it and their unmet needs are known.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q21 to Q23, Q25 to Q28
Time limit
Within 10 business days of consent (our standard)
Step 11

Practitioner

Describe each behaviour of concern.

Write what an observer can see and hear, not what you think it means. Record how often, how long and how intense it is, using a scale you name. Record early warning signs, how it ends, who is at risk and how seriously. Rate the risk of harm.

Result
Anyone can recognise and count each behaviour, and the risk is rated.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q29 to Q32
Time limit
Before the assessment report is due (our standard)
Step 12

Practitioner

Work out the function of each behaviour.

Look at setting events, triggers and what follows the behaviour. Write one summary statement for each behaviour. Say what evidence supports it and what would show it wrong. Say which other explanations you ruled out. Name a skill or behaviour that could meet the same need.

Result
Each behaviour has a testable function and a replacement skill.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q33 to Q38
Time limit
Before the assessment report is due (our standard)
Step 13

Practitioner

Map the participant's other supports and services.

List every NDIS and other support the participant uses: health, mental health, education, housing, justice, day and community services. Record what each does, who to contact and what it does when the behaviour happens. Say how they should fit together and what protocol each needs. With the participant's consent, ask each service to agree.

Result
We know every service and what each must do for the plan to work across them.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q44, Q45
Time limit
Before the assessment report is due (our standard)
Step 14

Warning. Apart from a single emergency use, a regulated restrictive practice used without authorisation breaks a condition of registration for the provider using it (Behaviour Support Rules, s 9(2)(a)). It can also harm the participant.

Practitioner

List every restrictive practice now in use.

Include any practice, regulated or not, and any practice in an earlier plan. Record who uses it, where, how often and since when. Record whether it is authorised and whether it is in a current plan. If you see a practice that could cause serious harm, such as a restraint that restricts breathing: call 000 if anyone is in danger, tell the person to stop, and tell the Service Manager the same day. If a regulated restrictive practice is in use without authorisation, tell the implementing provider in writing the same day. Then start PRO-SBS-05 Reportable Incidents Involving the Use of a Restrictive Practice Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support); the implementing provider notifies the Commission of its own use, and the Quality Manager decides whether it is also reportable by us. If you think a regulated restrictive practice may be needed in the plan (FRM-SBS-03 Q43), tell the Service Manager and start PRO-SBS-02 Restrictive Practices Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support) now, before the plan is drafted. Do not recommend a restrictive practice in the report.

Result
Every practice in use is on record with its status, and this report adds none.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q39 to Q43
Time limit
Same day for a practice that could cause serious harm. Otherwise before the assessment report is due (our standard)
Step 15

Practitioner

Write the assessment report.

Finish the recommendations in this order: changes to the environment; skills and replacement behaviours; proactive strategies; response strategies. Add the data each implementing provider should collect, the training they need, and chances for the participant to join community activities and learn new skills. Say whether an automated tool was used. Give the report its number. Set the date to revisit it.

Result
The report is complete and ready for checking.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q8, Q46 to Q53, Q56, Q57
Time limit
Within 49 days of the engagement date (our standard)
Step 16

Clinical Supervisor

Check the assessment report.

Check that consent is valid, a health cause was looked at, each function rests on evidence and the sources are listed. Check that no restrictive practice is recommended. Sign the sign-off block, or send the report back with the changes needed.

Result
The report is signed off, or returned with reasons.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q58
Time limit
Within 3 business days of receiving it (our standard)
Step 17

Practitioner

Go through the findings with the participant.

Use their way of communicating. Say what you found and what you recommend. Ask what they think. Write down any disagreement in their words. Share the findings with others only as the participant agreed.

Result
The participant has heard the findings and said what they think.
Record
FRM-SBS-03 Q54, Q55
Time limit
Within 5 business days of step 16 (our standard)

Write the plan

Step 18

Practitioner

Consult each implementing provider.

With the participant's consent, meet each provider that will carry out the plan. Ask what the plan can ask of them in their setting, who does what, what data they can collect and what training they need. Write down each answer. Consult while you write. Do not wait for the draft.

Result
Each implementing provider has been heard before the plan is drafted.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 Q11
Time limit
Before you finish the draft (our standard)

Step 19

Warning. A plan copied from another participant, or written on a template that misses an item the Commission's checklist requires, puts wrong strategies into practice and can break the Rules.

Practitioner

Draft the plan on a permitted, complete template.

Use the Commission's current template, our own approved template that holds every item in the Commission's plan checklist, or the template the state or territory authorising body requires (Behaviour Support Rules, section 23(1)). Check the Commission's website on the day you start for the current checklist and template edition. Write strategies from this participant's assessment report only. Cover every item in the plan content check (FRM-BSP-02 Q13). Give the participant chances to join community activities and learn new skills. Record each source you used. For each regulated restrictive practice, write the protocol the Commission's checklist requires. For a chemical restraint, copy the medication, dose, route and frequency exactly from the prescriber's current order and name the prescriber and the date of the order; you never decide or change a dose.

Result
A complete draft exists on a permitted template.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 Q1 to Q6
Time limit
Within 5 business days of step 16, alongside step 17 (our standard)
Step 20

Practitioner

If the draft includes, or may include, a regulated restrictive practice:

Check that the restrictive practice process is complete.

PRO-SBS-02 Restrictive Practices Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support) was started at step 14, when a practice first looked likely. Check now that the consultation, the notice of intention in a form the participant can understand, the risks, the alternatives and the state or territory authorisation route are all recorded. Result
The practice has been consulted on, noticed and authorised, or it is taken out of the draft.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 Q7, Q8
Time limit
Before the plan is finalised (our standard, giving effect to Behaviour Support Rules, s 20(2) and s 20(4))
Step 21

Practitioner

Give the draft to the participant.

Give it in a form they understand, such as plain words, pictures or a spoken summary. Go through it with them. Offer an independent advocate. Ask what they want changed. Write down their view, and any disagreement in their words. Change the draft where the change keeps them safe. If they still disagree, tell the Clinical Supervisor.

Result
The participant has seen the draft and said what they think.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 Q9, Q10
Time limit
Within 1 business day of finishing the draft (our standard)
Step 22

Practitioner

Send the draft to each implementing provider.

With the participant's consent, send the draft for consideration and written acceptance. Ask for an answer within 5 business days. Ask each provider to say yes, yes with changes, or no, and why.

Result
Each implementing provider has the draft and a date to answer.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 Q11
Time limit
Within 1 business day of finishing the draft (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 1Policy C1

Step 23

Practitioner

Record each provider's answer.

Chase any provider that has not answered by business day 3. If a provider asks for a change that keeps the participant safe, change the draft and tell every provider what changed. If a provider declines, or has not answered by business day 5, see If it goes wrong.

Every provider's answer, or its silence, is on record.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 Q12

Chase at 3 business days. Close at 5 business days after sending (our standard)

Step 24

Clinical Supervisor

Check the final draft.

Check the draft against every item in the plan content check (FRM-BSP-02 Q13, built from the Commission's checklist). The plan is cleared for finalising, or returned with reasons.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 Q13, Q14

Within 5 business days of receiving it, or 2 business days for an interim plan (our standard)

The plan is in force from the date of signing.

FRM-BSP-02 Q15

Within 1 business day of the Clinical Supervisor's clearance at step 24 (our standard). Give the plan to the participant and, with consent, to others.

Give the participant their plan in a form they understand, with the help they chose. With consent, give a copy to each person in the support network and each implementing provider. Tell each person to remove the old version. Record who got it, how and when.

Everyone who should have the plan has the current version, and the participant knows what it says.
Record
FRM-BSP-02 Q16

The participant: the same day as step 25. Each implementing provider: within 1 business day of step 25 (our standard)

If a regulated restrictive practice is used outside the plan, follow PRO-SBS-05 Reportable Incidents Involving the Use of a Restrictive Practice Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support)
The participant disagrees with the planWrite their view in their words. Offer an independent advocate. Tell them they can complain under PRO-FBK-01 Feedback and Complaints Management Procedure. If the disagreement is about a restrictive practice, PRO-SBS-02 sets what happens next
You are worried about a colleague or a managerTell the Clinical Supervisor. If it is about the Clinical Supervisor, tell the Service Manager, who uses the substitute (PRO-SBS-01 Decision table 4). If it is about the Service Manager, tell the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive, or about a sole Practitioner's own work, tell the Clinical Supervisor or phone the NDIS Commission on 1800 035 544. If you think a participant has been abused, neglected or restrained unlawfully, follow PRO-INC-01 Incident Management Procedure and PRO-SGD-01 Violence, Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation and Discrimination Procedure the same day
The participant leaves us or changes providerFollow PRO-SUP-04 Transitions to or from a Provider Procedure. With consent, give the new provider the current plan and the assessment report. Mark the row ended. Never delete it
The Practitioner is no longer considered suitableStop all assessment and plan work at once and tell the Service Manager. The Service Manager gives the work to another suitable Practitioner within 2 business days. The Clinical Supervisor checks the work already done before anyone relies on it. The due dates do not move
The system is downUse paper copies of FRM-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessment Report Template and FRM-BSP-02 Behaviour Support Plan Cover Sheet and Lodgement Record. The Service Manager enters them within 2 business days of the system coming back

8Done means

  • The assessment report is complete, signed off by the Clinical Supervisor and gone through with the participant.
  • The plan is finalised and in force, on a permitted template that holds every item in the Commission's checklist, with the Practitioner's endorsement.
  • Each implementing provider was consulted, was sent the draft and has an answer on record.
  • The participant has their plan in a form they understand.
  • A plan with a regulated restrictive practice has been through PRO-SBS-02 Restrictive Practices Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support) and lodged with the Commissioner, and the confirmation is filed.
  • Handover has started under PRO-SBS-03 Supporting the Implementation of the Behaviour Support Plan Procedure.
  • These records now exist:
    • the assessment report, FRM-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessment Report Template
    • the cover sheet, FRM-BSP-02 Behaviour Support Plan Cover Sheet and Lodgement Record
    • the consent record, FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form
    • the consultation record, FRM-SBS-02 Restrictive Practice Consultation Record, where a practice is involved
    • a complete row in REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register.

9Quick card

134 words
  • If anyone is in danger, call 000 first, and tell anyone using a practice that could cause serious harm to stop (step 14)
  • Only a Practitioner the Commissioner considers suitable assesses or writes (step 5)
  • No consent, no assessment: ask the participant first (step 6)
  • Ask for a health review before you decide what a behaviour means (step 7)
  • Work out every due date the day you set the engagement date (step 4)
  • A restrictive practice goes in a plan only through PRO-SBS-02 (step 20)
  • Send the draft to each implementing provider and wait for each answer (step 22)
  • Give the participant their plan in a form they understand, the day it is final (step 26)
  • The Practitioner lodges every plan with a regulated restrictive practice within 5 business days of finalising (step 27)

docs.html:
1Purpose

The result: every provider, worker and supporter who will carry out a participant's has helped shape it. Each understands the reasons for it, has been in it and can get help when something gets in the way.

This procedure gives effect to POL-SBS-04 Supporting the Implementation of the Behaviour Support Plan Policy, C1 to C13. Only a specialist behaviour support provider uses it. A provider that only carries out plans uses POL-BSP-04 Behaviour Support Plan Implementation Policy.

the : a day other than a Saturday, a Sunday or a public holiday in the state or territory where the participant lives.

2When and who

PRO-BSP-03 Functional Behaviour Assessments and Behaviour Support Plans Procedure sets how a plan is drafted, accepted and . This procedure starts where that one hands over. Start it at each of these points:

  • A plan, interim or comprehensive, is given out (steps 1 to 15 and 18 to 20).
  • A worker is new, absent, relief or agency (step 16).
  • A new version of the plan is given out (step 17, then any other step the change touches).
  • A provider raises a , or a check-in is due (steps 21 to 24).

The practitioner is the who holds the plan. The practitioner does every step except steps 26 to 28. Only an NDIS behaviour support practitioner explains the plan, teaches its strategies and checks how well people carry them out. Other staff may book sessions, send papers and file records.

The Service Manager copies the answers to REG-SBS-01 (step 26) and samples the records (step 28). The reads the records (step 27).

In a sole practitioner business, the practitioner holds the Service Manager and Chief Executive roles. The external Clinical Supervisor, engaged in writing and named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register, does step 27 and also step 28, the Service Manager's check on the practitioner's own work. The independent contact for concerns named there reads the sample.

An is any provider, registered or not, that delivers supports to the participant where the plan applies. Its is the person it names as your contact for the plan. The is the family, friends, carers, guardian and advocates the participant chooses.

A plan is given out when the participant, and with consent the support network and each implementing provider, hold the finished plan. PRO-BSP-03 does this within 1 business day of the plan being finalised.

The handover clock is 5 business days after the plan is finalised (our standard). It is 2 business days for an interim plan. Steps 5 to 13 are complete within the handover clock, for a first plan and for a new version. PRO-SBS-06 Interim Behaviour Support Plans Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support) and POL-SBS-07 use this clock for an interim plan and set no other handover time.

In this procedure:

  • The Restrictive Practices Rules means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.
  • The Incident Rules means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Incident Management and Reportable Incidents) Rules 2018.
  • A section number after either name, such as s 14, is a section of that instrument.

3Before you start

  • You know which plan this is, its number, its type (interim or comprehensive) and its version, from REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register.
  • You have the participant's consent record, FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form.
  • You have their communication preferences, FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form.
  • You have a copy of FRM-SBS-04 Behaviour Support Plan Handover and Training Record, and the you wrote for the plan.
  • For a plan with a , you know the state or territory where each practice will be used. You can open our note for that state or territory in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register, and you have a way to reach its authorising body.

4Watch out

  • A plan that contains a restrictive practice has not made the practice authorised. comes from the state or territory. If you tell a provider that a practice is authorised and it is not, a worker may use it without authority. The participant may be harmed, and the use is a reportable incident.
  • Do not use this template, an old copy or memory for a state or territory rule. The rules change and differ in each place. Take the rule from our dated . A wrong rule leads to a wrong use.
  • Telling is not understanding. A person who nods may not have understood. A worker who misunderstands a strategy can use it wrongly and harm the participant.
  • Attendance is not competence. A worker who signed the sheet may still be unable to carry out the plan. Their provider trains and observes them against the plan and confirms it to you in writing. You observe a sample, and every worker who will apply a physical restraint protocol.
  • Tell the provider in writing what an untrained worker may and may not do. A continuous environmental or mechanical restraint that the plan directs stays in place as the plan says, and the provider's supervisor tells the worker its conditions of use at the start of their first shift. An untrained worker does not apply a physical restraint technique or an as-needed practice, and calls the provider's on-call manager instead. Removing a continuous restraint because a worker is untrained can itself cause the harm the plan prevents.
  • Share only what the participant agreed to. Sharing the plan without consent breaches privacy. It can put the participant at risk if a family member is the concern.
  • Teach a physical technique only if you are qualified to teach it. A badly taught technique can injure the participant or the worker.
  • This procedure is not an emergency response. If someone is hurt or in danger, call 000 and follow the emergency steps in the plan.

5Steps

Prepare

Step 1

The practitioner

Open a record for each implementing provider, and name a contact at each.

Read the providers listed in REG-SBS-01 as consulted on the plan. Ask the participant, or the person who decides for them, whether any provider is missing: a day program, respite, transport or a community support. Ask the support coordinator too, if there is one. If a provider is missing, tell the Service Manager the same business day, and consult that provider as PRO-BSP-03 sets before you go on. Open FRM-SBS-04 for each provider and answer Q1 and Q4.

Result
Every provider that will carry out the plan has a record and a named implementation contact.
Record
FRM-SBS-04 Q4
Time limit
Before the handover starts (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 1Policy C1Record it on: →Form, question 4Form Q4→Form, question 1Form Q1

Step 2

Warning. Sharing a plan without consent breaches privacy. It can put the participant at risk if a family member is the concern.

The practitioner

Check what the participant has agreed to share, and with whom.

Read the sharing consent in REG-SBS-01 and the participant's FRM-INF-01. Write each person and provider the participant agreed to, and any limit. If a person decides for the participant by law, ask that person and also ask the participant. If the consent is missing or has run out, ask now and record the answer before you share anything.

Result
You know who may see the plan and who may not.
Record
FRM-SBS-04 Q7
Time limit
Before you share any part of the plan (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 2Policy C2Record it on: →Form, question 7Form Q7

Step 3

The practitioner

Confirm that each implementing provider has accepted its part in the plan.

Read the provider's answer in REG-SBS-01. It comes from PRO-BSP-03, where the provider was consulted, sent the draft and asked to accept. Copy the answer to Q10. If a provider has not accepted, use the first item under "If it goes wrong".

Result
You know which providers accepted, and which did not.
Record
FRM-SBS-04 Q10
Time limit
Before the handover starts (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 1Policy C1Record it on: →Form, question 10Form Q10

Step 4

Warning. A plan that contains a restrictive practice has not made the practice authorised. A wrong rule given to a provider can lead to unauthorised use and harm.

The practitioner

If the plan includes a regulated restrictive practice:

Find the authorisation rule and the current authorisation status for each practice.

For each practice, find the state or territory where it will be used. Open our note for that state or territory in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register. Its last-checked date must be within the last 6 months, and the note must have been re-checked after any change the NDIS Commission or the state or territory body has announced (PRO-SBS-02 Restrictive Practices Procedure (Specialist Behaviour Support), step 2; our standard). If it is not, or there is no note, ask the to bring it up to date under PRO-SBS-02 step 3. Go no further until they have. Then read the participant's authorisation outcome in REG-SBS-01 (authorisation): the authorising body, its reference, the date, the conditions and the end date. Write the note's last-checked date and the outcome. If anything is unclear, ask the authorising body, and tell no one the practice is authorised until you can confirm it. If the state or territory prohibits the practice, use Decision table 1.

Result
You know the rule for each practice where it will be used, and its status for this participant, from dated sources.
Record
FRM-SBS-04 Q14 and Q15
Time limit
Before the handover starts. Check again if more than 5 business days pass before it starts (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 6Policy C6Record it on: →Form, question 14Form Q14→Form, question 15Form Q15

Hand over the plan

Step 5

Warning. A plan explained only to the adults around the participant can leave the participant not knowing why things are changing. They may then refuse the strategies or feel punished.

The practitioner

Explain the plan to the participant first, in the way they understand best.

The participant already holds the plan. Now explain its reasons. Use the supports in FRM-RGT-01. Offer a trusted supporter, a break or two shorter sessions. Say what the behaviour tells us the participant needs, what the plan aims for and why each strategy is there. Ask what the participant thinks and write their words. If a person decides for the participant by law, explain to that person too. If the participant does not seem to follow, try another way and record what you tried.

Result
The participant has heard the reasons for their plan and has had a say.
Record
FRM-SBS-04 Q8, Q9 and Q11
Time limit
Within the handover clock (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 3Policy C3Record it on: →Form, question 8Form Q8→Form, question 9Form Q9→Form, question 11Form Q11

Step 6

The practitioner

If the participant agreed to share the plan with a family member, friend, carer, guardian or advocate:

Explain the plan to each person in the support network whom the participant agreed to.

Give the same reasons you gave the participant. Ask what they have seen work. Tell them their part in the plan, if they have one. Do not share anything the participant asked you to keep back. Use an interpreter or an accessible format if the person needs one.

Result
The people the participant chose understand the reasons for the plan.
Record
FRM-SBS-04 Q11
Time limit
Within the handover clock (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 3Policy C3Record it on: →Form, question 11Form Q11

Step 7

The practitioner

Explain the plan to the managers and workers of each implementing provider.

Hold a handover meeting with the implementation contact and every worker you can bring in. Ask the contact to include casual, relief and agency workers. Cover what the behaviour tells us, what the plan aims for and why each strategy is there. List everyone who took part, and everyone who will carry out the plan and was not there.

Result
Each implementing provider has heard the reasons, and you know who is still to be reached.
Record
FRM-SBS-04 Q5, Q6 and Q11
Time limit
Within the handover clock (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 3Policy C3Record it on: →Form, question 5Form Q5→Form, question 6Form Q6→Form, question 11Form Q11

Step 8

Warning. A person who nods may not have understood. A worker who misunderstands a strategy can use it wrongly and harm the participant.

The practitioner

Check that each person understood, by asking them to .

Ask each person to tell you in their own words what the behaviour is telling us and what they will do. For a strategy, ask them to show you. If a person cannot, explain again in a different way and check again. Name anyone who needs more help.

Result
You know who understood and who needs more help.
Record
FRM-SBS-04 Q12
Time limit
At the end of the same session (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 4Policy C4Record it on: →Form, question 12Form Q12

Step 9

The practitioner

Give each person the instructions and guidance for the plan.

For the participant, give a version in their own format. For workers, give a one page strategy card with the plan's steps in order. The card carries: the early signs; the proactive steps; the response steps in order; what never to do; the conditions on any restrictive practice and its authorisation status; who to call; and the plan's version number and date. Reissue the card with every new version of the plan. For the support network, give what to do at home. Write the version number and the date on each item. Ask the provider to keep the card where its workers see it at the start of a shift. Ask its supervisor to go through the card with each worker at the start of their first shift on the plan, and to keep doing so until the worker is trained.

Result
Each person holds the current instructions and knows where to find them.
Record
FRM-SBS-04 Q13
Time limit
At the handover (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 5Policy C5Record it on: →Form, question 13Form Q13

Step 10

The practitioner

If the plan includes a regulated restrictive practice:

Explain to each provider how each practice is authorised and the conditions on its use.

Give the implementation contact the , one page for each practice. The written notice you give under PRO-SBS-02 step 27 is this summary, so check it is current and give it now if you have not. It names the authorising body, who applies, the consent needed, the evidence to lodge, the date the authorisation ends and the conditions on use. The conditions say when the practice may be used, what must be tried first, for how long, by whom and what is not allowed. Say that a practice used outside the conditions is not authorised. Go through it with the managers and workers who will use the practice, and ask them to say it back.

Result
The provider knows the rule and the conditions for each practice, and who must apply.
Record
FRM-SBS-04 Q15 and Q16
Time limit
At the handover (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 6Policy C6Record it on: →Form, question 15Form Q15→Form, question 16Form Q16

Step 11

The practitioner

If the plan includes a regulated restrictive practice:

Agree who does what to get or keep each authorisation.

For each practice, write its status using the first column of Decision table 1. The choices run from approved to not required. For each open item, write the action, its owner and its due date. Use Decision table 1 to decide what to tell the provider. Do not tell anyone a practice is authorised until you have seen the evidence.

Result
Every practice has a status and every open item has an owner and a date.
Record
FRM-SBS-04 Q17
Time limit
At the handover. Each action falls due within 10 business days, unless the authorising body's own timetable is longer (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 6Policy C6Record it on: →Form, question 17Form Q17

Step 12

The practitioner

Agree with the implementation contact who holds each reporting duty.

Give the contact the and go through it duty by duty. If you gave a written notice under PRO-SBS-02 step 27, start from it and add anything missing. Duty 1: report each use of a regulated restrictive practice to the NDIS Commissioner every month. Use the Commissioner's approved form (Restrictive Practices Rules s 14(1)(a) and (2)). While a short term approval from the state or territory is in force, report every 2 weeks instead (s 14(1)(b)). The Commission expects the monthly report within 5 business days after the end of the month, and expects the provider to activate the lodged plan and lodge evidence of authorisation in the NDIS Commission Portal (Commission guidance, not the Rules). Duty 2: keep a written record of each use for 7 years (s 15). Duty 3: lodge evidence of authorisation with the Commissioner as soon as reasonably practicable after a use (s 9(2)(b)). Duty 4: tell us when circumstances change, so we can review the plan (s 10(2)(b)), and tell us of any emergency or unauthorised use within 1 business day (our standard). Duty 5: if a practice is used and no plan covers it, take all reasonable steps to have an interim plan within 1 month. Take the same steps for a comprehensive plan within 6 months (s 11 to s 13). Duty 6: report a use that is not authorised, or not in line with the plan, as a reportable incident. The time runs from when the provider becomes aware. Notify the Commissioner within 24 hours of becoming aware where the incident involves the death, serious injury, abuse or neglect, unlawful sexual or physical contact or sexual misconduct of a participant, or an unauthorised restrictive practice that resulted in harm; otherwise within 5 business days (Incident Rules s 16, s 20 and s 21; Commission guidance on harm). Advise the 24 hour route for any injury or medical check, and whenever in doubt. If the plan has no restrictive practice, say that it allows none and that any use must be reported. If the provider is not registered, say that these duties bind registered providers. Tell it that the law of the state or territory and the NDIS Code of Conduct still apply to it. If the plan contains a regulated restrictive practice and the provider is not registered for supports that involve one (the Registration Rules s 7(2)), tell the Clinical Supervisor the same business day and start the concern route in PRO-SBS-04 Behaviour Support Plan Monitoring and Review Procedure (Decision table 3). If you are unsure what else applies, ask the NDIS Commission. Ask who holds each duty and write the name and role.

Result
The provider knows each duty and a named person holds it.
Record
FRM-SBS-04 Q18 and Q19
Time limit
At the handover (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 7Policy C7Record it on: →Form, question 18Form Q18→Form, question 19Form Q19

Train and coach

Step 13

Warning. A worker who only attended may still be unable to carry out the plan. The wrong response at the wrong moment can harm the participant.

The practitioner

Train each person who will carry out the plan in the plan's strategies.

Train the lead workers and the supervisor of each implementing provider, including those who cover casual, relief and agency workers. With the participant's consent, train the family and friends who help. Where the participant agrees, let them show what helps them in their own way. Start with a short knowledge check about this plan, and repeat it at the end. Teach the positive strategies first: changes to the place and routine, communication, teaching new skills, reinforcing what works, and early warning signs. Then teach the response strategies, recording data and what to do after an incident. Explain, demonstrate, and let each person practise and get feedback. Give the provider's supervisor a competence checklist for this plan, one line for each strategy. Ask the supervisor to train every other worker against it, to observe each worker, and to confirm to you in writing which workers are competent and which still need coaching. If the plan has a restrictive practice, explain its protocol, and leave any physical technique to step 18 unless you are qualified to teach it. If someone else teaches part of the session, check what they teach against the plan. Ask for feedback at the end.

Result
The provider's lead workers and supervisor have been taught this participant's strategies, the supervisor holds the competence checklist, and you hold the scores and feedback.
Record
FRM-SBS-04 Q5, Q20, Q21, Q22 and Q24
Time limit
Within the handover clock (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 8Policy C8Record it on: →Form, question 5Form Q5→Form, question 20Form Q20→Form, question 21Form Q21→Form, question 22Form Q22→Form, question 24Form Q24

Step 14

The practitioner

Observe a sample of workers carrying out the strategies, and every worker who will apply a physical restraint protocol.

Ask the provider for its written confirmation of the workers it has trained and observed against the checklist. Then go on shift, where the participant agrees, and watch a sample: at least one worker from each shift pattern, and every worker who will apply a physical restraint protocol. Where it is not safe or fair to watch with the participant, watch a practice run. Never ask a worker to use a restrictive practice so that you can watch it. Mark each worker you watched, for each strategy, as can do without help, or needs coaching. Base the mark on what you saw, not on who attended. Tell the worker what you saw, kindly and plainly. If the sample shows gaps the provider's confirmation did not, tell the provider's manager in writing and widen the sample.

Result
You know that the provider's confirmation holds, which workers you watched, and who needs coaching.
Record
FRM-SBS-04 Q23
Time limit
Within 10 business days after the training, and again at each check-in (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 8Policy C8Record it on: →Form, question 23Form Q23

Step 15

The practitioner

If a worker needs coaching on any strategy:

Coach each worker who needs it.

Go back to the strategy. Show it again and let the worker try it with feedback. Ask a skilled colleague at the provider to mentor the worker between your visits. Watch again as in step 14. Write the gaps and the plan to close them, with an owner at each end. If a worker still needs coaching after 2 rounds, tell the provider's manager in writing. Ask the Clinical Supervisor whether the strategy is workable as written.

Result
Each worker can carry out the strategies, or an agreed action has an owner and a date.
Record
FRM-SBS-04 Q23 and Q25
Time limit
Within 10 business days after each time you watch, until the worker can do each strategy without help (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 8Policy C8Record it on: →Form, question 23Form Q23→Form, question 25Form Q25

Step 16

Warning. A worker who has not been trained and who uses a restrictive practice can injure the participant. The use would also be outside the plan.

The practitioner

If a worker who will carry out the plan was absent from training, is new, or is relief or agency:

Catch up the worker.

Ask each provider to tell you when a new or relief worker is rostered on the plan. Give the worker the strategy card and the reasons for the plan. The provider's supervisor goes through the card with the worker at the start of their first shift, trains and observes them against the competence checklist, and confirms it to you in writing. Offer the worker a place in your next training or coaching session, and include them in the sample at step 14 where you can. Tell the provider's manager in writing what the worker may and may not do until they are trained: a continuous environmental or mechanical restraint that the plan directs stays in place as the plan says; the worker does not apply a physical restraint technique or an as-needed practice, and calls the provider's on-call manager instead.

Result
The worker has been taught and observed, or the provider has been told in writing what the worker may and may not do until then.
Record
FRM-SBS-04 Q5 and Q6
Time limit
Offer within 10 business days after you are told (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 9Policy C9Record it on: →Form, question 5Form Q5→Form, question 6Form Q6

Step 17

The practitioner

If a new version of the plan has been given out after a review or a barrier:

Brief everyone who holds the plan on what changed.

Tell the participant first, then the support network the participant agreed to, then each implementing provider. Say what changed and why. Give the new instructions and guidance. Ask each holder to take away the old versions and confirm they have. Train again on any changed strategy, using steps 13 and 14. Where the new version changes nothing but the version number and the review date, give every holder notice of the new number and date, ask them to replace the old version, make one FRM-SBS-04 entry and do not retrain. PRO-SBS-04 Behaviour Support Plan Monitoring and Review Procedure sets how a plan is reviewed.

Result
Everyone who holds the plan has the new version and understands the change. The old versions are gone.
Record
FRM-SBS-04 Q13
Time limit
Within the handover clock (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 5Policy C5Record it on: →Form, question 13Form Q13

Oversee training in a restrictive practice

Step 18

The practitioner

If the plan includes a regulated restrictive practice and we recommend that workers be trained in its safe use:

Recommend the training in writing and say what it must cover.

Name the practice in the plan's own words. Say the training must cover the conditions of use, what must be tried first and the shortest time. Say it must cover who may use it, how to stop and what to do afterwards. Say it must teach only what is in the plan. Ask who will deliver it and what qualifies the trainer to teach it. A physical technique is taught only by a person qualified to teach it. Ask for the trainer's outline before the training.

Result
The provider knows what the training must teach and has been asked for the trainer's outline.
Record
FRM-SBS-04 Q26
Time limit

Step 19

The practitioner

Review the trainer's outline against the plan.

Read the outline line by line against the plan. Check that it teaches the practice as the plan describes it, with the plan's conditions, and nothing the plan does not contain. Mark it as matches the plan, needs changes, or not acceptable. Tell the provider in writing, with each change needed. If it is not acceptable, ask the Clinical Supervisor to join you. Tell the provider that we do not accept it as training in this plan.

The outline matches the plan, or the provider holds our written list of changes.
Record

Within 5 business days after you get the outline, and before the training takes place (our standard)

The practitioner

Confirm the training was delivered as agreed to every worker who needs it.

Ask for the attendance record. Where you can, watch part of a session. List each worker still to be trained and tell the provider in writing. If what was taught differs from the plan, tell the Clinical Supervisor the same business day and ask the provider to correct it.

Result
You hold evidence that the training matched the plan, and you know who still needs it.
Record
FRM-SBS-04 Q28
Time limit
Within 10 business days after the training (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 10Policy C10Record it on: →Form, question 28Form Q28

Support the providers over time

Step 21

The practitioner

Offer ongoing support and advice, and agree the next check-in.

Give the implementation contact, and the support network the participant agreed to, your contact details. Say you reply within 2 business days. Say that if someone is unsafe they call 000 and follow the plan's emergency steps. They can also call the provider's on-call manager. You are not an emergency service. Agree the first check-in within 10 business days after the handover. After that, hold the check-in with each monitoring check under PRO-SBS-04 Behaviour Support Plan Monitoring and Review Procedure, so that one visit makes one record, and at least every 3 months while the plan is in force.

Result
Each provider knows how to reach you and when you will next be in touch.
Record
FRM-SBS-04 Q31
Time limit
At the handover. Reply within 2 business days of each request. Check in at least every 3 months (our standard)

Puts into action: ←Policy, commitment 11Policy C11Record it on: →Form, question 31Form Q31

Step 22

The practitioner

If a provider or a support network member raises a barrier, or you find one at a check-in:

Agree an action for each barrier.

At each check-in ask what is getting in the way: staffing, time, training, the place, equipment or the plan itself. Write each barrier in the person's words. Give advice. Agree an action, its owner and its due date. Never leave a barrier without an owner.

Result
Each barrier has advice, an action, an owner and a due date.
Record

At the contact. Each due date falls within 10 business days, unless a plan review is needed (our standard)

The practitioner

If an action agreed at step 22 is now due:

Follow up each action on its due date.

Ask the owner what was done. Write the result. If the action was not done or did not work, agree a new action, or go to step 24.

Each action is done, replaced or sent on.

Send it to the right process, using Decision table 2.

Tell the Clinical Supervisor the same business day if a plan is not being followed. Do the same if a practice has been used outside the plan or without authorisation. Tell the implementing provider which process you started.

Read the records for each plan with the practitioner.

Read every FRM-SBS-04 made since the last session. Ask whether each person understood. Ask whether the authorisation rule came from its source. Ask whether workers were watched and not only trained, and whether barriers are moving. Write what you found and any action for the practitioner.

Sample the records and the register.

Pick 5 plans, or all of them if we hold fewer than 5. Trace each from REG-SBS-01 to its FRM-SBS-04 records. Check each time limit in this procedure. The outcomes use the words of PRO-SBS-02 Decision table 3. A single emergency use of a practice that is not authorised is reportable too (Incident Rules s 16).

7If it goes wrong

IfThen
A provider has not accepted its part (Q10 shows declined or no reply)Read the decision recorded in REG-SBS-01 under PRO-BSP-03. Do not tell the participant's team that the provider accepted. Ask the provider's senior manager what stops it, within 5 business days. If a change to the plan would answer it, tell the Clinical Supervisor the same business day, because a change is a new version. If not, within 10 business days tell the participant, and their support coordinator if they agree, that this provider cannot carry out the plan, and ask what they want to do. Still give the provider the authorisation summary and the reporting summary, because its duties under the Restrictive Practices Rules do not depend on its accepting the plan
The participant does not want the plan explained, or will not agree to share it with a person or providerStop and do not share. Explain what that person will not see and what it means for carrying out the plan. Offer another way: a shorter version, a different supporter or another day. If a provider that must carry out the plan cannot be given it, tell the Clinical Supervisor the same business day and write it as a barrier at Q29
A provider does not answer or cannot attendKeep trying, in more than one way, and record each attempt. When the attempts meet the test in PRO-SBS-04 Decision table 3 for a provider that cannot be engaged effectively, tell the Clinical Supervisor and start the concern route there. PRO-SBS-04 sets the notice to the NDIS Commissioner
You cannot confirm a state or territory authorisation ruleAsk the authorising body or the NDIS Commission. Tell no one the practice is authorised. Tell the provider "not confirmed" and the date by which you will confirm it
A worker will not, or cannot, carry out a strategy after 2 rounds of coachingTell the provider's manager in writing. Ask the Clinical Supervisor whether the strategy is workable as written. If it is not, start a plan review under PRO-SBS-04
A worker missed the training or joins lateUse step 16
A provider is using an old version of the plan, or the plan's review date has passedGive the current version the same business day and ask the provider to remove the old one (step 17). If the review is overdue, tell the Clinical Supervisor and start a plan review under PRO-SBS-04
Someone is in danger or hurt during a contactStop. Call 000 if the danger is now. Help the provider's workers follow the emergency steps in the plan. Then use Decision table 2
You will miss a time limit in this procedureTell the Service Manager as soon as you know, and the implementation contact before the limit ends. Write the reason and the new date at Q3. Nobody can extend a time limit that the law sets
You learn that a restrictive practice was used outside the plan or without authorisationUse Decision table 2 the same business day. The provider reports its own use to the Commissioner. We advise and review
The participant changes provider, or a new provider joinsTreat the new provider as an implementing provider. Start at step 1 for it. Tell the old provider in writing that the plan no longer applies to it
You are awayThe Service Manager gives the work to another suitable practitioner within 2 business days. The Clinical Supervisor or you hand over the file. In a sole practitioner business, the Clinical Supervisor names a covering practitioner in writing before any planned leave. Tell each implementation contact who to call within 1 business day (our standard)
You are worried about a colleague, the Clinical Supervisor or a managerThis includes pressure to say a practice is authorised when it is not, to skip a step, or to sign for training that did not happen. Tell the Clinical Supervisor. If the concern is about the Clinical Supervisor, tell the Chief Executive. If it is about the Chief Executive, or the Chief Executive is the practitioner, tell the independent contact for concerns named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register. You may always tell the NDIS Commission. Nobody may punish you for raising it. POL-SGD-01 Violence, Abuse, Neglect, Exploitation and Discrimination Policy applies if the concern is about harm to a person
Systems are downUse a paper copy of FRM-SBS-04. Enter it within 2 business days after the system is back (our standard)

8Done means

  • The participant has heard the reasons for their plan, in their own way, and has had a say.
  • The support network the participant chose has been told, and nobody else has been given the plan.
  • Each implementing provider has accepted its part, holds the current instructions and guidance, and has said the reasons back.
  • Each regulated restrictive practice has a dated authorisation status, an owner for each open item, and a named person who holds each reporting duty.
  • Each worker has been taught and observed by their provider, or by us, and, where needed, coached. Workers not yet ready have been named to their provider in writing, with what they may and may not do until then.
  • Any restrictive practice training has been checked against the plan, and the provider knows who is still to be trained.
  • Each barrier has an action, an owner and a due date.
  • FRM-SBS-04 is signed and filed, and REG-SBS-01 is up to date.

9Quick card

121 words
  • Do not tell anyone a restrictive practice is authorised until you have seen the evidence (step 4)
  • Share the plan only with whom the participant agreed (step 2)
  • Explain the plan to the participant first, in their way (step 5)
  • Ask each person to say it back, and explain again until they can (step 8)
  • Agree who holds each reporting duty at each provider (step 12)
  • Observe a sample of workers, and every worker who will apply a physical restraint protocol. Attendance is not competence (step 14)
  • Review any restrictive practice training against the plan before it runs (step 19)
  • Catch up every new or absent worker (step 16)
  • Give every barrier an action, an owner and a date (step 22)

form.intro:
Use this form to record what we explained, taught and agreed with the people who carry out a participant's . It is the proof that we handed the plan over, trained people in it and kept supporting them.

The who holds the plan completes it. Open one running record for each implementing provider for each version of the plan, and one for the support network. Add a dated entry for each contact. A contact is any meeting, session, visit or call listed at question 2, and questions 2 and 3 are answered for each entry. Questions 1 and 4 are answered once per record.

Answer Sections A, B and I every time. Answer the other sections when the contact covered them. The heading of each section says when. If you do not know an answer, write "Not known" and the date you will find out. Never leave it blank.

When | Complete these questions

Handover (the first contact with a provider or the support network): questions 1 to 13; 14 to 17 where the plan has a ; 18, 19 and 29 to 32.

Training, coaching or mentoring: questions 1 to 6, 20 to 25 and 29 to 32.

Catch-up for a new or absent worker: questions 1 to 6, 13, 23, 25 and 29 to 32.

Restrictive practice training oversight: questions 1 to 4 and 26 to 32.

Check-in or advice on a barrier: questions 1 to 4 and 29 to 32.

Briefing on a changed plan: questions 1 to 4, 11 to 13, 17 where the authorisation changed, and 29 to 32. For a version that changes only the version number and the review date: questions 1 to 4, 13 and 31.

Have these ready:

  • the plan, with its number, version and the date it was given out, from REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register
  • the participant's consent record, FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form
  • the participant's communication preferences, FRM-RGT-01 Communication, Advocacy and Support Preferences Form
  • the you wrote for the plan
  • for a plan with a regulated restrictive practice, our note for each state or territory of use (kept in REG-QMS-03 Compliance Obligations Register)
  • for the same plan, the participant's authorisation outcome from REG-SBS-01
  • the and the reporting summary.

These six answers decide what you do next. Do that step before you close the record.

  • A provider at question 10 that has not accepted its part: use the first item under "If it goes wrong" in PRO-SBS-03.
  • A practice at question 17 that is not approved: use Decision table 1 in PRO-SBS-03.
  • "Needs coaching" at question 23: go to PRO-SBS-03 step 15.
  • "Needs changes" or "Not acceptable" at question 27: go to PRO-SBS-03 step 19.
  • Any barrier at question 29: give it an action, an owner and a due date at question 30 (PRO-SBS-03 step 22).
  • Any choice at question 32 other than "nothing further": go to PRO-SBS-03 step 24.

What happens next: you sign the record and file it within 2 business days of the contact. The Service Manager then copies the answers named in the question protocol to REG-SBS-01 within 2 business days. PRO-SBS-03 Supporting the Implementation of the Behaviour Support Plan Procedure sets each step.

When systems are down, use a paper copy. Enter it within 2 business days after the system is back.
form.privacy:
We collect this information to show that the people who support the participant understand the behaviour support plan and can carry it out. It also shows us where they need more help.

The record holds information about the participant, about workers of the implementing provider, and about family or friends who took part. We keep it for at least 7 years (our standard; the law sets 7 years for the provider that uses the practice). The practitioner, the and the Service Manager read it. An auditor or the NDIS Commission may read it where the law allows.

We give an implementing provider only the parts about its own workers and the actions it agreed to. We share with the support network only what the participant agreed to on FRM-INF-01 Consent to Collect, Use and Share Information Form.

If you are the participant, or a person named in this record, you can ask to see what it says about you. You can ask us to correct it. POL-INF-01 Information Management Policy sets how we store and protect it.
form.after:
• The practitioner files the record in the participant's file within 2 business days of the contact (our standard).
  • The Service Manager copies the answers named in the question protocol to REG-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Plan Register. They do this within 2 business days after the practitioner files the record (our standard).
  • The practitioner sends the implementation contact one consolidated copy of questions 5, 6, 10, 17 to 19, 23, 25 and 30 when the handover closes, and again when a later section closes, within 5 business days. The practitioner sends the person who decides for the participant by law, and with the participant's consent their support coordinator, questions 13, 17, 25 and 30 only: what was given, the authorisation status and the actions. The implementing provider keeps its own training records, for example on FRM-BSP-05 Behaviour Support Plan Training and Sign-Off Record.
  • Anything chosen at question 32 goes to its process on the same business day. PRO-SBS-03 step 24 names each process.
  • The Clinical Supervisor reads the records for each plan at the practitioner's next supervision session and notes it on FRM-SBS-01 Behaviour Support Clinical Supervision Record.
  • The Service Manager samples the records every 3 months. In a sole practitioner business, the external Clinical Supervisor does this and the independent contact for concerns named in REG-GOV-01 Delegations Register reads the sample.

register.proves:
This register is the one running record of every [Provider name] writes. It has three sheets. On the plan sheet each row is one plan version. It shows when we were engaged and who wrote the plan. It shows what the participant agreed to and which accepted the plan. It shows whether the plan reached the Commissioner on time and when it is next due for review. On the practice sheet each row is one in one plan, keyed on the plan number in col A, and holds the answers FRM-SBS-02 Restrictive Practice Consultation Record routes here, with every status the practice has held. On the incident review sheet each row is one review under FRM-SBS-06 Restrictive Practice Incident Review Record of an emergency or unauthorised use, keyed on the plan number in col A.

"Behaviour Support Rules" here means the National Disability Insurance Scheme (Restrictive Practices and Behaviour Support) Rules 2018.

  • Indicators evidenced: s 40 (1) to s 40 (6). The register also holds the plan dates and records that s 39, s 41, s 42, s 43 and s 44 rely on. Those threads write to the columns marked with their indicators.
  • Legal basis: the Behaviour Support Rules. Sections 17 and 18 say who writes. Section 19 sets time limits. Section 20 says how plans are developed and section 21 what they contain. Sections 22 to 24 cover review, form and lodgement.
  • Retention: keep each row for 7 years from the day the plan is superseded or ends (our standard). We set it to match the 7 years in section 15(3) of the Behaviour Support Rules for records of the use of a regulated restrictive practice.
  • Other law can require longer, for example for records about a child. For a participant under 18, keep the row until they turn 25 or for 7 years, whichever is later (our standard pending state law). Check REG-INF-02 Records Retention and Disposal Register and the law of [state or territory] before any row is destroyed.

Columns H and I are worked out and never typed over. Columns AB, AC, AD and AW are filled only when col Z lists a regulated restrictive practice, and summarise the practice sheet. Columns AN to AP are filled only when col AM is yes. Columns AR to BA are filled from the forms named in the Filled from column. The practice sheet columns RP-A to RP-R are filled from FRM-SBS-02, one row per practice per plan. The incident review sheet columns IR-A to IR-O are filled from FRM-SBS-06, one row per review; col AZ summarises them.
register.entry:
1. The Service Manager opens the row and keeps it. A sole Practitioner does both. Open the row on the day we confirm the referral (our standard).
  2. Use one row for each plan version. A new version is a new row. Link it to the one it replaces in col D and col BD.
  3. The Practitioner gives each answer to the Service Manager within 1 of recording it on the form. The forms are FRM-SBS-03 Functional Behaviour Assessment Report Template and FRM-BSP-02 Behaviour Support Plan Cover Sheet and Lodgement Record for the plan sheet, and FRM-SBS-02 Restrictive Practice Consultation Record for the practice sheet. The Service Manager enters it within 2 business days of the stage (our standard).
  4. Columns that hold a list (col R, col Z, col AC, col AD, col AG, col AK, col AW and col BB, and practice sheet cols RP-P and RP-R) take a new dated line for each change. Never overwrite a line. An authorisation status is never typed over: every status the practice has held stays visible with its date.
  5. Never overwrite or delete an entry. A correction is a new version of the row, with the date, your name and the reason.
  6. Never type over a worked-out date. To change the engagement date in col F, record the reason and the name of the who agreed.
  7. When systems are down, use the paper forms. The Service Manager enters them within 2 business days of the system coming back.
  8. When a row is about the work of the Service Manager or the Practitioner who keeps it, the Chief Executive holds it. When it is about the Chief Executive, the holds it. In a sole practitioner provider the Practitioner keeps every row, and the outside Clinical Supervisor reviews them every month under How we review.
  9. The practice sheet is the second sheet of this register: one row per regulated restrictive practice per plan, keyed on the plan number in col A, with cols RP-A to RP-R. Open a practice row when col Z first lists or proposes the practice. The incident review sheet is the third sheet: one row per FRM-SBS-06 review, keyed on col A, with cols IR-A to IR-O; open a row when a review starts and summarise it in col AZ. A small provider can keep the other list columns on a further sheet in the same way; each line carries the plan number from col A.

A row is closed only when all of these are true:

  • the plan has been replaced by a later version that is in force, or the plan has ended, or the participant has left us, and col BD says which
  • every lodgement is done and recorded in col AO
  • every open line in col BB is done, or has moved to REG-QMS-01 Continuous Improvement Register with an owner and a due date
  • the Service Manager has checked the row and recorded the closing date.

register.rows: The rows are the data. They are kept in the workbook or system built to this specification, not in this document. The register has three sheets: the plan sheet (one row per plan version, cols A to BF), the practice sheet (one row per regulated restrictive practice per plan, cols RP-A to RP-R, keyed on col A) and the incident review sheet (one row per FRM-SBS-06 review, cols IR-A to IR-O, keyed on col A). Where a plan sheet cell would otherwise hold a list of practices or reviews, the second or third sheet holds the detail and the plan sheet cell summarises it. Every column name on the plan sheet is kept stable, because other documents cite the columns by name.
